name: Familial Clubfoot with or without Associated Lower Limb Anomalies

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical and Familial Diagnostic Criteria for Familial Clubfoot

criteria.description: Presence of congenital talipes equinovarus (clubfoot) deformity at birth
Positive family history of clubfoot or related lower limb anomalies in first-degree relatives
Presence or absence of associated lower limb anomalies such as limb length discrepancy or foot hypoplasia
Exclusion of syndromic or neuromuscular causes of clubfoot by clinical and genetic evaluation

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of congenital clubfoot deformity with a positive family history and exclusion of syndromic causes
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Genetic counseling and detailed family pedigree analysis are recommended to support diagnosis.

pathognomonic.notes: Fixed foot inversion, adduction, and plantarflexion present at birth

pathognomonic.symptomName: Medial foot crease and cavus foot deformity
pathognomonic.notes: Characteristic medial crease and high arch of the foot
searchTerms: inner foot crease with high arch
medial foot fold and cavus foot
foot crease plus high arch deformity

common.notes: Underdevelopment of calf muscles on affected side
Restricted upward movement of the ankle joint
Shortening of the affected lower limb compared to contralateral side
Reduced passive mobility of foot joints

occasional.notes: Shortening and tightening of the Achilles tendon

occasional.symptomName: Mild foot deformities in unaffected limb
occasional.notes: Subclinical or mild deformities in contralateral foot
searchTerms: mild foot deformities on unaffected side
minor foot shape changes in other foot
slight foot abnormalities in opposite limb

occasional.notes: Mild delay in walking or standing due to foot deformity

rare.notes: Developmental dysplasia of the hip in affected individuals
Rare coexisting neuromuscular features in some families
Occasional skin dimples or creases over deformity

imaging: X-ray showing talocalcaneal coalition and abnormal foot bone alignment
MRI in complex cases to evaluate soft tissue and muscle hypoplasia
genetic: Familial inheritance pattern consistent with autosomal dominant or multifactorial inheritance
Genetic testing to exclude syndromic causes such as arthrogryposis or distal arthrogryposis
other: Physical examination revealing fixed equinovarus deformity
Pedigree analysis showing multiple affected family members

distinguishingFeatures: Isolated foot deformity without associated limb anomalies
Multiple joint contractures beyond the foot

redFlags: Progressive worsening of foot deformity despite treatment
Presence of neurological deficits or muscle weakness
Associated systemic anomalies suggesting syndromic diagnosis
references: Orphanet: Familial Clubfoot with or without Associated Lower Limb Anomalies, ORPHA:199315
Dobbs MB, Gurnett CA. Update on clubfoot: etiology and treatment. Clin Orthop Relat Res. 2009 May;467(5):1146-53.
Dobbs MB, Morcuende JA, Gurnett CA. Treatment of idiopathic clubfoot: an historical review. Iowa Orthop J. 2000;20:59-64.
